## Issue - resolve: Additional knip errors missed in PR #1853 ## Why is this change needed? There were remaining errors that were missed during the review of https://github.com/liam-hq/liam/pull/1853. This PR addresses the remaining knip configuration issues that were not caught in the previous review. ## What would you like reviewers to focus on? - Removal of unused `langfuse` dependency while preserving `langfuse-vercel` - Cleanup of unnecessary `ignoreUnresolved` configuration in knip.jsonc ## Testing Verification Knip configuration has been tested to ensure no false positive errors remain. ## What was done ### 🤖 Generated by PR Agent at 2a5658cd915a0bc4efde07322c0ff5a16b97a4c5 - Removed unused `langfuse` dependency from `package.json` - Cleaned up unnecessary `ignoreUnresolved` entries in `knip.jsonc` - Streamlined knip configuration for accuracy and maintainability ## Detailed Changes
Relevant files
Dependencies
package.json
Remove unused langfuse dependency from package.json

  • Deleted the langfuse dependency from the dependencies list
  • Kept langfuse-vercel dependency intact

p_title: Implement CallInvoker as replacement for JSDispatcher
p_body:
## Description
Implements a new CallInvoker API on IReactContext, and some additional helpers on ReactContext, which modifies how users access the jsi::Runtime.

### Type of Change
- Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- This change requires a documentation update

### Why
The current implantation of JSDispatcher is thread based.  This worked well on the old arch where the JS runtime ran on a dedicated thread.  However, in the new architecture there are cases where the JS runtime can end up running on the UI thread.  This means that that existing usages of JSDispatcher that are being used to directly interact with the JS runtime, could run into cases where they attempt to access the JS runtime on the JS thread while the runtime is being used on the UI thread.

### What
Modifies the new arch code path to no longer create a JSDispatcher with a MessageQueueThread, but instead create a MessageQueueThread directly.  This uses more shared code from core.  

Previously we exposed JSDispatcher to gain access to the JS thread, and a JsiRuntime property on ReactContext, which allowed access to the jsi::Runtime object.  -- Although that API should only have been accessed from the JS thread.

With this change I'm replacing JSDispatcher with a new CallInvoker API.  This property exposes the same [CallInvoker](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/76ce7890141f22ba75cf62806762179be3c8cfa9/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/callinvoker/ReactCommon/CallInvoker.h) that react-native uses.  CallInvoker allows access to the jsi::Runtime in a more controlled way where it is only accessible on the stack during a callInvoker callback.  This prevents access to the jsi::Runtime in an unsafe manner.

With this change RNW will align with core, by restricting access to the jsi::Runtime to locations where it is valid to use it.

## Changelog
Should this change be included in the release notes: Yes

Add a brief summary of the change to use in the release notes for the next release.
IReactContext.JSDispatcher, IReactContext.JsiRuntime, and ExecuteJsi are no longer valid in new architecture, and these APIs are deprecated for old architecture.  These will be removed in a future release.
Replacing those APIs is a new IReactContext.CallInvoker API.  -- Although most applications should use ReactContext.CallInvoker for ease of use.  The CallInvoker allows safe access to the jsi::Runtime and aligns with how you access the jsi::Runtime on other platforms.

old:
```c++
  ExecuteJsi(reactContext, [](jsi::Runtime &runtime) {
    ... // Interact with jsi::Runtime here
  });
```

new:
```c++
  reactContext.CallInvoker()->invokeAsync([](jsi::Runtime &runtime) {
    ... // Interact with jsi::Runtime here
  });
```

In addition, a new optional parameter on module initializers has been added.  Module initializers can now take a jsi::Runtime& argument that can be used to synchronously interact with the jsi::Runtime during module initialization.

old:
```c++
REACT_INIT(Initialize)
void Initialize(msrn::ReactContext const &reactContext) noexcept {
  ExecuteJsi(reactContext, [](jsi::Runtime &runtime) {
    ... // Interact with jsi::Runtime here
  });
}
```

new:
```c++
REACT_INIT(Initialize)
void Initialize(msrn::ReactContext const &reactContext, jsi::Runtime& runtime) noexcept {
  ... // Interact with jsi::Runtime here
}
```

p_title: feat: support to set an empty context to the Task
p_body:
Closes #2789

TD;LR

Treat 'falsy' issue while setting context to a Task

----

Currently, the `Task.context` is other tasks whose outputs will be used as context for the task. The default value is None which is a 'falsy' Python value. 
For a Crew `None` means: get the context from all previous tasks outputs. This creates a limitation, because we currently have no way to explicitly say, “this task should have no additional context.

This PR address this issue by allowing us to set empty value in a Task's context. From now on, any falsy Python value (like `None`, `[]`, or `False`) will be treated as "no context should be used" for the task

Bumps [@babel/core](https://github.com/babel/babel/tree/HEAD/packages/babel-core) from 7.26.10 to 7.27.1.
Release notes

Sourced from @​babel/core's releases.

v7.27.1 (2025-04-30)

Thanks @​kermanx and @​woaitsAryan for your first PRs!

:eyeglasses: Spec Compliance

  • babel-parser
    • #17254 Allow using of as lexical declaration within for (@​JLHwung)
    • #17230 Disallow get/set in TSPropertySignature (@​JLHwung)
  • babel-parser, babel-types
    • #17193 Stricter TSImportType options parsing (@​JLHwung)

:bug: Bug Fix

  • babel-plugin-proposal-destructuring-private, babel-plugin-proposal-do-expressions, babel-traverse
    • #17137 fix: do expressions should allow early exit (@​kermanx)
  • babel-helper-wrap-function, babel-plugin-transform-async-to-generator
    • #17251 Fix: propagate argument evaluation errors through async promise chain (@​magic-akari)
  • babel-helper-remap-async-to-generator, babel-plugin-transform-async-to-generator
    • #17231 fix apply()/call() annotated as pure (@​Lacsw)
  • babel-helper-fixtures, babel-parser
    • #17233 Create ChainExpression within TSInstantiationExpression (@​JLHwung)
  • babel-generator, babel-parser
    • #17226 Fill optional AST properties when both estree and typescript parser plugin are enabled (Part 2) (@​JLHwung)
  • babel-parser
    • #17224 Fill optional AST properties when both estree and typescript parser plugin are enabled (Part 1) (@​JLHwung)
    • #17080 Fix start of TSParameterProperty (@​JLHwung)
  • babel-compat-data, babel-preset-env
    • #17228 Update firefox bugfix compat data (@​JLHwung)
  • babel-traverse
    • #17156 fix: Objects and arrays with multiple references should not be evaluated (@​liuxingbaoyu)
  • babel-generator
q_body:
Bumps [antd](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design) from 5.25.0 to 5.25.4.
Release notes

Sourced from antd's releases.

5.25.4

  • 💄 Tweak Select selected item background in dark theme to make it easier to identify. #53956 @​afc163
  • ⌨️ Timeline now uses ol instead of ul to meet HTML semantic requirements. #53944 @​fnoopv
  • 🐞 Fix Drawer mask does not fade out when changing from true to false. #53955 @​afc163
  • 🐞 Fix Input.Search does not support onPressEnter. #53898 @​codingories
  • 🛠 Remove !important style syntax from Checkbox. #53953 @​doandevhere
  • TypeScript
    • 🤖 Fix Descriptions.Item span property type. #53913 @​DDDDD12138
  • 💄 调整 Select 选中项在暗色模式下的背景色，使其更容易识别。#53956 @​afc163
  • ⌨️ Timeline 使用 ol 代替 ul 以符合 html 语义要求。#53944 @​fnoopv
  • 🐞 修复 Drawer mask 从 true 改为 false 时没有渐出的问题。#53955 @​afc163
  • 🐞 修复 Input.Search 不支持 onPressEnter 的问题。#53898 @​codingories
  • 🛠 移除 Checkbox 的 !important 样式语法。#53953 @​doandevhere
  • TypeScript
    • 🤖 修正 Descriptions.Item span 属性类型。#53913 @​DDDDD12138

5.25.3

  • 🐞 Fix Typography.Text delete property not updating. #53861 @​codingories
  • 🐞 Fix the Statistic.Timer as a subcomponent of Tooltip could not display text prompts properly. #53888 @​jin19980928
  • 🐞 Fix the style setting of the Upload component did not take effect in more types. #53877 @​QuentinHsu
  • 💄 Fix the residual focus style after clicking Tabs. #53901
  • 🐞 修复 Typography.Text delete 属性无法更新的问题。

Release notes

Sourced from rollup's releases.

v4.40.2

4.40.2

2025-05-06

Bug Fixes

  • Create correct IIFE/AMD/UMD bundles when using a mutable default export (#5934)
  • Fix execution order when using top-level await for dynamic imports with inlineDynamicImports (#5937)
  • Throw when the output is watched in watch mode (#5939)

Pull Requests

  • #5934: fix(exports): avoid "exports is not defined" ReferenceError (@​dasa)
  • #5937: consider TLA imports have higher execution priority (@​TrickyPi)
  • #5939: fix: watch mode input should not be an output subpath (@​btea)
  • #5940: chore(deps): update dependency vite to v6.3.4 [security] (@​renovate[bot])

q_body:
Bumps [antd](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design) from 5.25.0 to 5.25.4.
Release notes

Sourced from antd's releases.

5.25.4

  • 💄 Tweak Select selected item background in dark theme to make it easier to identify. #53956 @​afc163
  • ⌨️ Timeline now uses ol instead of ul to meet HTML semantic requirements. #53944 @​fnoopv
  • 🐞 Fix Drawer mask does not fade out when changing from true to false. #53955 @​afc163
  • 🐞 Fix Input.Search does not support onPressEnter. #53898 @​codingories
  • 🛠 Remove !important style syntax from Checkbox. #53953 @​doandevhere
  • TypeScript
    • 🤖 Fix Descriptions.Item span property type. #53913 @​DDDDD12138
  • 💄 调整 Select 选中项在暗色模式下的背景色，使其更容易识别。#53956 @​afc163
  • ⌨️ Timeline 使用 ol 代替 ul 以符合 html 语义要求。#53944 @​fnoopv
  • 🐞 修复 Drawer mask 从 true 改为 false 时没有渐出的问题。#53955 @​afc163
  • 🐞 修复 Input.Search 不支持 onPressEnter 的问题。#53898 @​codingories
  • 🛠 移除 Checkbox 的 !important 样式语法。#53953 @​doandevhere
  • TypeScript
    • 🤖 修正 Descriptions.Item span 属性类型。#53913 @​DDDDD12138

5.25.3

  • 🐞 Fix Typography.Text delete property not updating. #53861 @​codingories
  • 🐞 Fix the Statistic.Timer as a subcomponent of Tooltip could not display text prompts properly. #53888 @​jin19980928
  • 🐞 Fix the style setting of the Upload component did not take effect in more types. #53877 @​QuentinHsu
  • 💄 Fix the residual focus style after clicking Tabs. #53901
  • 🐞 修复 Typography.Text delete 属性无法更新的问题。

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:

There were remaining errors that were missed during the review of https://github.com/liam-hq/liam/pull/1853. ### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#800)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:
    -   **the `diff` package on npm now includes its own TypeScript type definitions**. Users who previously used the `@types/diff` npm package from DefinitelyTyped should remove that dependency when upgrading JsDiff to v8.

+openapi-postgres:

### Changes 🏗️

- Implement `BackendAPI.onWebSocketConnect(..)`

- Improve reliability and reactivity of `/library/agents/[id]`:
  - Refresh page data and (re)subscribe and on WebSocket (re)connect
  - Break up multi-action hooks into smaller parts to reduce unnecessary re-renders and requests
  - Reduce duplicate requests

- Use `onWebSocketConnect` in `useAgentGraph` as well

- Tidy up `autogpt-server-api/client.ts` a bit

### Checklist 📋

- [x] I have made a test plan

  - Go to `/library/agents/[id]`
  - Run the agent
    - [x] -> UI should update normally with execution updates
  - Suspend your computer, or restart the backend (or WS server) to break the connection

  - Run the agent again

q_body: There are a few UI bugs on the builder that this PR addresses. ### Changes 🏗️ Fix these UI issues: * (screenshot attached above) Key-value input width was unintentionally maxed out due to a stale CSS rule. * When multiple executions within the same node are running, we pick the latest status, making one running and one completed execution displayed as completed. * No balance errors were executed, only displayed while at least one node execution was triggered, while this can be done directly when the execution request is triggered. * Run & Stop button glitch: it's still showing as stopped when the graph is still running, this is due to way the UI code tracks execution in the node-level, instead of graph level. ### Checklist 📋 #### For code changes: - [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description - [x] I have made a test plan - [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan: - [x] Manual tests on the described behaviours.

# Ticket: Implement Core EVM RPC Wrappers & Basic Reads (Polygon Plugin)

**Ticket Type:** Dev Ticket  
**Priority:** P1  
**Epic:** Implement Polygon Plugin MVP  
**Assignee:** Harsh Modi  
**Reporter:** AI Assistant

This ticket has been completed. - Integrated wrapper functions for standard EVM JSON-RPC methods.

# Dependencies Cleanup

## Summary
This PR addresses critical dependency management issues in the monorepo that were causing build failures and CLI functionality problems.

## Problem
- Unnecessary dependencies in the monorepo were causing version conflicts
- Old/outdated package versions were being installed, breaking compatibility
- CLI was not working properly due to dependency issues
- Several packages that should not be in the monorepo were included (elevenlabs, redpill)

## Changes Made
- Removed unnecessary dependencies from monorepo root
- Cleaned up outdated package versions
- Removed `elevenlabs` package (should not be in monorepo)
- Removed `redpill` package (should not be in monorepo)
- Fixed CLI dependency conflicts
- Streamlined package.json dependencies

## Impact
- CLI now works properly
- Eliminates version conflicts between packages
- Cleaner monorepo structure
- Improved build reliability
- Better dependency isolation

## Breaking Changes
None - this is purely a cleanup that improves stability.

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#800)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:
    -   **the `diff` package on npm now includes its own TypeScript type definitions**. Users who previously used the `@types/diff` npm package from DefinitelyTyped should remove that dependency when upgrading JsDiff to v8.

        Note that the transition from the DefinitelyTyped types to JsDiff's own type definitions includes multiple fixes and also removes many exported types previously used for `options` arguments to diffing and patch-generation functions. (Th

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#800)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:
    -   **the `diff` package on npm now includes its own TypeScript type definitions**. Users who previously used the `@types/diff` npm package from DefinitelyTyped should remove that dependency when upgrading JsDiff to v8.

        Note that the transition from the DefinitelyTyped types to JsDiff's own type definitions includes multiple fixes and also removes many exported types previously used for `options` arguments to diffing and patch-generation functions. (Th

## Issue - resolve: Additional knip errors missed in PR #1853 ## Why is this change needed? There were remaining errors that were missed during the review of https://github.com/liam-hq/liam/pull/1853. This PR addresses the remaining knip configuration issues that were not caught in the previous review. ## What would you like reviewers to focus on? - Removal of unused `langfuse` dependency while preserving `langfuse-vercel` - Cleanup of unnecessary `ignoreUnresolved` configuration in knip.jsonc ## Testing Verification Knip configuration has been tested to ensure no false positive errors remain. ## What was done ### 🤖 Generated by PR Agent at 2a5658cd915a0bc4efde07322c0ff5a16b97a4c5 - Removed unused `langfuse` dependency from `package.json` - Cleaned up unnecessary `ignoreUnresolved` entries in `knip.jsonc` - Streamlined knip configuration for accuracy and maintainability ## Detailed Changes

package.json
Remove unused langfuse dependency from package.json

p_title: Cast float time to int in Span.to_proto
p_body:
🛠 DevTools 🛠

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/B-Step62/mlflow/pull/15733?quickstart=1) #### Install mlflow from this PR ``` # mlflow pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/15733/merge # mlflow-skinny pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/15733/merge#subdirectory=skinny ``` For Databricks, use the following command: ``` %sh curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/HEAD/dev/install-skinny.sh | sh -s pull/15733/merge ```

### What changes are proposed in this pull request? While testing review app, I found `mlflow.search_traces()` doesn't handle traces written from Review App properly. ``` TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer File , line 1 ----> 1 mlflow.search_traces(run_id=my_session.mlflow_run_id) ``` After closer look, the start time of the span is set to be `float` somehow. This is a bug in review app side (they log json directly), but adding casting in mlflow side to fix it immediately. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [ ] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. You can skip the rest of this section. - [ ] Yes. ### Release Notes

<details>

### [`v4.1.5`](https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#415---2025-04-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/compare/v4.1.4...v4.1.5)

##### Added

-   Support using `@tailwindcss/upgrade` to upgrade between versions of v4.\* ([#​17717](https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/17717))

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#800)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:
    -   **the `diff` package on npm now includes its own TypeScript type definitions**. Users who previously used the `@types/diff` npm package from DefinitelyTyped should remove that dependency when upgrading JsDiff to v8.

## Issue - resolve: Additional knip errors missed in PR #1853 ## Why is this change needed? There were remaining errors that were missed during the review of https://github.com/liam-hq/liam/pull/1853. This PR addresses the remaining knip configuration issues that were not caught in the previous review. ## What would you like reviewers to focus on? - Removal of unused `langfuse` dependency while preserving `langfuse-vercel` - Cleanup of unnecessary `ignoreUnresolved` configuration in knip.jsonc ## Testing Verification Knip configuration has been tested to ensure no false positive errors remain. ## What was done ### 🤖 Generated by PR Agent at 2a5658cd915a0bc4efde07322c0ff5a16b97a4c5 - Removed unused `langfuse` dependency from `package.json` - Cleaned up unnecessary `ignoreUnresolved` entries in `knip.jsonc` - Streamlined knip configuration for accuracy and maintainability ## Detailed Changes

package.json
Remove unused langfuse dependency from package.json           
frontend/apps/app/package.json

  • Kept langfuse-vercel dependency intact
  • Streamlined package management by removing unused package

 # Release History

-Major changes happened in this version as the client library switched to using the new AI Foundry data-plane REST APIs.
-(TODO: Add link). Please see updated samples.
+There have been significant updates with the release of version 1.0.0b11, including breaking changes.
+Please see new samples and package README.md file.
 
-### Breaking changes
+### Features added
 
-* Endpoint URL is now needed to construct the `AIProjectClient`, instead of using the factory method
-`.from_connection_string`. Find this endpoint URL in your AI Foundry project page.
-* Agent operations that were previously part of the `azure.ai.projects` package have moved out to a separate new package
-`azure-ai-assistants` with a client named `AssistantClient`. See INSERT URL HERE for more information. You can get the `AssistantClient` by calling `.assistant.get_client()` method on your `AIProjectClient`.
-* Import `PromptTemplate` from `azure.ai.projects` instead of `azure.ai.projects.prompts`.
-* Several changes to `.connections` operations. Please see new connection samples.
-* TODO: `.evaluations` methods ..
+* `.deployments` methods to enumerate AI models deployed to your AI Foundry project.
+* `.datasets` methods to upload documents and reference them. To be used with Evaluations.
+* `.indexes` methods to handle your Search Indexes.
 
-### Features added
+### Breaking changes
 
-* `.deployment` methods to enumerate the deployed AI models in your AI Foundry project.
-* `.datasets` method to upload documents and reference them. These documents will be used to augment the capability
-of your selected LLM (RAG pattern).
-* `.indexes` methods to handle your AI search indexes and search queries, as part of RAG pattern.
-* TODO: `.red_team` methods ...
+* Azure AI Foundry project endpoint is now required to construct the `AIProjectClient`. Find it in your AI Foundry Project
+overview page. The factory method `from_connection_string` was removed.
+* Agents are now implemented in a separate package `azure-ai-agents`. Continue using the ".agents" operations on the
+`AIProjectsClient` to create, run and delete agents, as before. However there have been some breaking changes in these operations.
+See [Agents package document and samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/ai/azure-ai-agents) for more details.

+AI models deployed to the Project's AI Services. This is in addition to the existing option to get an `AzureOpenAI` client for one of the connected Azure OpenAI services.
+* Import `PromptTemplate` from `azure.ai.projects` instead of `azure.ai.projects.prompts`.
 
 ### Sample updates

p_body: ## Description - When updating the file content, the dev tools tab synchronizes this change immediately. ## Related Issues ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Release - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Testing ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Synchronize dev tools tab with file content updates, handle file events, and update dependencies. > > - **Behavior**: > - Dev tools tab now synchronizes immediately with file content updates in `file-tree.tsx` and `index.tsx`. > - Handles file events for add, remove, and change to update file list and content. > - **File Handling**: > - `FileTree` component in `file-tree.tsx` now accepts `files` prop and uses `ResizeObserver` for width. > - `buildFileTree` function memoized to optimize performance. > - `loadNewContent` function added to `index.tsx` to update file content on change events. > - **Styling**: > - Removed `z-10` class from `PopoverContent` in `color-background.tsx`, `input-color.tsx`, and `text-selected.tsx`. > - **Dependencies**: > - Updated various dependencies in `bun.lock`, including `eslint`, `react`, and `next`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=onlook-dev%2Fonlook&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 854099927a7f871a82a4838914fe58163f71f466. <details>

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#800)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:
    -   **the `diff` package on npm now includes its own TypeScript type definitions**. Users who previously used the `@types/diff` npm package from DefinitelyTyped should remove that dependency when upgrading JsDiff to v8.

        Note that the transition from the DefinitelyTyped types to JsDiff's own type definitions includes multiple fixes and also removes many exported types previously used for `options` arguments to diffing and patch-generation functions. (Th

+
+def is_valid_tool(obj):
+    from crewai.tools.base_tool import Tool
+
+    if isclass(obj):
+        try:
+            return any(base.__name__ == "BaseTool" for base in getmro(obj))
+        except (TypeError, AttributeError):
+            return False
+
+    return isinstance(obj, Tool)
+
+
+def extract_available_exports(dir_path: str = "src"):
+    """
+    Extract available tool classes from the project's __init__.py files.
+    Only includes classes that inherit from BaseTool or functions decorated with @tool.
+
+    Returns:
+        list: A list of valid tool class names or ["BaseTool"] if none found
+    """
+    try:
+        init_files = Path(dir_path).glob("**/__init__.py")
+        available_exports = []
+
+        for init_file in init_files:
+            tools = _load_tools_from_init(init_file)
+            available_exports.extend(tools)
+
+        if not available_exports:
+            _print_no_tools_warning()
+            raise SystemExit(1)
+
+        return available_exports
+
+    except Exception as e:
+        console.print(f"[red]Error: Could not extract tool classes: {str(e)}[/red]")
+        console.print(
+            "Please ensure your project contains valid tools (classes inheriting from BaseTool or functions with @tool decorator)."
+        )
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+
+def _load_tools_from_init(init_file: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    """
+    Load and validate tools from a given __init__.py file.
+    """
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("temp_module", init_file)
+
+    if not spec or not spec.loader:
+        return []
+
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules["temp_module"] = module
+
+    try:
+        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+
+        if not hasattr(module, "__all__"):
+            console.print(
+                f"[bold yellow]Warning: No __all__ defined in {init_file}[/bold yellow]"
+            )
+            raise SystemExit(1)
+
+        return [
+            {
+                "name": name,
+            }
+            for name in module.__all__
+            if hasattr(module, name) and is_valid_tool(getattr(module, name))
+        ]
+
+    except Exception as e:
+        console.print(f"[red]Warning: Could not load {init_file}: {str(e)}[/red]")
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+    finally:
+        sys.modules.pop("temp_module", None)
+
+
+def _print_no_tools_warning():
+    """
+    Display warning and usage instructions if no tools were found.
+    """
+    console.print(
+        "\n[bold yellow]Warning: No valid tools were exposed in your __init__.py file![/bold yellow]"
+    )
+    console.print(
+        "Your __init__.py file must contain all classes that inherit from [bold]BaseTool[/bold] "
+        "or functions decorated with [bold]@tool[/bold]."
+    )
+    console.print(
+        "\nExample:\n[dim]# In your __init__.py file[/dim]\n"
+        "[green]__all__ = ['YourTool', 'your_tool_function'][/green]\n\n"
+        "[dim]# In your tool.py file[/dim]\n"
+        "[green]from crewai.tools import BaseTool, tool\n\n"
+        "# Tool class example\n"
+        "class YourTool(BaseTool):\n"
+        '    name = "your_tool"\n'
+        '    description = "Your tool description"\n'
+        "    # ... rest of implementation\n\n"
+        "# Decorated function example\n"
+        "@tool\n"
+        "def your_tool_function(text: str) -> str:\n"
+        '    """Your tool description"""\n'
+        "    # ... implementation\n"
+        "    return result\n"
+    )

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>kpdecker/jsdiff (diff)</summary>

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#800)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/7.0.0...v8.0.0)

-   [#​580](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/580) **Multiple tweaks to `diffSentences`**:
    -   tokenization no longer takes quadratic time on pathological inputs (reported as a ReDOS vulnerability by Snyk); is now linear instead
    -   the final sentence in the string is now handled the same by the tokenizer regardless of whether it has a trailing punctuation mark or not. (Previously, "foo. bar." tokenized to `["foo.", " ", "bar."]` but "foo. bar" tokenized to `["foo.", " bar"]` - i.e. whether the space between sentences was treated as a separate token depended upon whether the final sentence had trailing punctuation or not. This was arbitrary and surprising; it is no longer the case.)
    -   in a string that starts with a sentence end, like "! hello.", the "!" is now treated as a separate sentence
    -   the README now correctly documents the tokenization behaviour (it was wrong before)
-   [#​581](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/581) - **fixed some regex operations used for tokenization in `diffWords` taking O(n^2) time** in pathological cases
-   [#​595](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/595) - **fixed a crash in patch creation functions when handling a single hunk consisting of a very large number (e.g. >130k) of lines**. (This was caused by spreading indefinitely-large arrays to `.push()` using `.apply` or the spread operator and hitting the JS-implementation-specific limit on the maximum number of arguments to a function, as shown at https://stackoverflow.com/a/56809779/1709587; thus the exact threshold to hit the error will depend on the environment in which you were running JsDiff.)
-   [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/596) - **removed the `merge` function**. Previously JsDiff included an undocumented function called `merge` that was meant to, in some sense, merge patches. It had at least a couple of serious bugs that could lead to it returning unambiguously wrong results, and it was difficult to simply "fix" because it was [unclear precisely what it was meant to do](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/issues/181#issuecomment-2198319542). For now, the fix is to remove it entirely.
-   [#​591](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/591) - JsDiff's source code has been rewritten in TypeScript. This change entails the following changes for end users:
    -   **the `diff` package on npm now includes its own TypeScript type definitions**. Users who previously used the `@types/diff` npm package from DefinitelyTyped should remove that dependency when upgrading JsDiff to v8.

There were remaining errors that were missed during the review of https://github.com/liam-hq/liam/pull/1853. p_title: Docs: Updated step 4 to remind user to grab the service_role key
p_body: ## Description Updated step 4 of the docs page to remind the developer during project setup to store the service_role key for later use. ## Related Issues None ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Documentation update - [ ] Release - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Testing None ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes None ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Update documentation to remind developers to grab the `service_role key` during project setup. > > - **Documentation**: > - Updated step 4 in `index.mdx` to remind developers to grab the `service_role key` during project setup for later use in step 7. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=onlook-dev%2Fonlook&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for b238512698fc9a5d18f5da182b7c553b8eea17ce. p_title: Docs: Updated step 4 to remind user to grab the service_role key
p_body: ## Description Updated step 4 of the docs page to remind the developer during project setup to store the service_role key for later use. ## Related Issues None ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Documentation update - [ ] Release - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Testing None ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes None ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Update documentation to remind developers to grab the `service_role key` during project setup. > > - **Documentation**: > - Updated step 4 in `index.mdx` to remind developers to grab the `service_role key` during project setup for later use in step 7. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=onlook-dev%2Fonlook&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for b238512698fc9a5d18f5da182b7c553b8eea17ce. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/onlook-dev/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed.
q_body: This reverts commit 6cba090c2c780aa62739b2f033da885a05ea4b8b. ## Description CSB new version exhibit too many unexpected behavior. Is not stable. ## Related Issues ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Release - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Testing ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Revert CodeSandbox API upgrade due to instability, downgrading `@codesandbox/sdk` and removing related code changes. > > - **Revert CodeSandbox API Upgrade**: > - Downgrade `@codesandbox/sdk` from `^1.1.0` to `^0.11.1` in `package.json` and `bun.lock`. > - Remove `userId` parameter from `SessionManager.start()` in `session.ts` and related API calls in `sandbox.ts`. > - Replace `WebSocketSession` with `SandboxSession` in `file-watcher.ts` and `session.ts`. > - Remove `shortenUuid` function from `id.ts` and its tests from `id.test.ts`. > - **Behavior Changes**: > - Remove user ID check in `main.tsx` for sandbox session start. > - Add `reconnect` logic in `main.tsx` for sandbox session. > - **Misc**: > - Reorganize imports in `color-popover.tsx` and `main.tsx`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=onlook-dev%2Fonlook&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 03940844d57c4a7a78a63502bc8ec4aa466d69d4. p_title: Docs: Updated step 4 to remind user to grab the service_role key
p_body: ## Description Updated step 4 of the docs page to remind the developer during project setup to store the service_role key for later use. ## Related Issues None ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Documentation update - [ ] Release - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Testing None ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes None ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Update documentation to remind developers to grab the `service_role key` during project setup. > > - **Documentation**: > - Updated step 4 in `index.mdx` to remind developers to grab the `service_role key` during project setup for later use in step 7. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=onlook-dev%2Fonlook&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for b238512698fc9a5d18f5da182b7c553b8eea17ce. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/onlook-dev/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed.

q_body: ## Description This PR fixes an issue where opening an image file in the dev tab displayed a random string instead of rendering the image preview. Changes - Detects image file types and renders them as images in the UI - Ensures non-image files continue to display as code ## Related Issues ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Release - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Testing ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes image rendering in dev tab by detecting and rendering image files correctly. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes image rendering in `DevTab` in `index.tsx` by detecting image file types and rendering them as images. > - Non-image files continue to display as code. > - **Functions**: > - Adds `getFileUrl()` and `getMimeType()` in `index.tsx` to handle image rendering. > - Updates `openFile()` in `index.ts` to detect binary files and convert them to base64. > - **Constants**: > - Adds `BINARY_EXTENSIONS` to `files.ts` for image file type detection. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=onlook-dev%2Fonlook&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for c5357d9f4974c6bba950d7667ed2cd813d4eff60. ---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>evanw/esbuild (esbuild)</summary>

### [`v0.25.4`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0254)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.3...v0.25.4)

-   Add simple support for CORS to esbuild's development server ([#​4125](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4125))

    Starting with version 0.25.0, esbuild's development server is no longer configured to serve cross-origin requests. This was a deliberate change to prevent any website you visit from accessing your running esbuild development server. However, this change prevented (by design) certain use cases such as "debugging in production" by having your production website load code from `localhost` where the esbuild development server is running.

    To enable this use case, esbuild is adding a feature to allow [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (a.k.a. CORS) for [simple requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS#simple_requests). Specifically, passing your origin to the new `cors` option will now set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header when the request has a matching `Origin` header. Note that this currently only works for requests that don't send a preflight `OPTIONS` request, as esbuild's development server doesn't currently support `OPTIONS` requests.

    Some examples:

    -   **CLI:**

            esbuild --servedir=. --cors-origin=https://example.com

    -   **JS:**

        ```js
        const ctx = await esbuild.context({})
        await ctx.serve({
          servedir: '.',
          cors: {
            origin: 'https://example.com',
          },
        })
        ```

    -   **Go:**

        ```go
        ctx, _ := api.Context(api.BuildOptions{})
        ctx.Serve(api.ServeOptions{
          Servedir: ".",
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

    In JavaScript, the special property name `__proto__` sets the prototype when used

        ```go
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

    In JavaScript, the special property name `__proto__` sets the prototype when used

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>evanw/esbuild (esbuild)</summary>

### [`v0.25.4`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0254)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.3...v0.25.4)

-   Add simple support for CORS to esbuild's development server ([#​4125](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4125))

    Starting with version 0.25.0, esbuild's development server is no longer configured to serve cross-origin requests. This was a deliberate change to prevent any website you visit from accessing your running esbuild development server. However, this change prevented (by design) certain use cases such as "debugging in production" by having your production website load code from `localhost` where the esbuild development server is running.

    To enable this use case, esbuild is adding a feature to allow [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (a.k.a. CORS) for [simple requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS#simple_requests). Specifically, passing your origin to the new `cors` option will now set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header when the request has a matching `Origin` header. Note that this currently only works for requests that don't send a preflight `OPTIONS` request, as esbuild's development server doesn't currently support `OPTIONS` requests.

    Some examples:

    -   **CLI:**

            esbuild --servedir=. --cors-origin=https://example.com

    -   **JS:**

        ```js
        const ctx = await esbuild.context({})
        await ctx.serve({
          servedir: '.',
          cors: {
            origin: 'https://example.com',
          },
        })
        ```

    -   **Go:**

        ```go
        ctx, _ := api.Context(api.BuildOptions{})
        ctx.Serve(api.ServeOptions{
          Servedir: ".",
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

    In JavaScript, the special property name `__proto__` sets the prototype when used

### [`v0.25.4`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0254)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.3...v0.25.4)

-   Add simple support for CORS to esbuild's development server ([#​4125](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4125))

    Starting with version 0.25.0, esbuild's development server is no longer configured to serve cross-origin requests. This was a deliberate change to prevent any website you visit from accessing your running esbuild development server. However, this change prevented (by design) certain use cases such as "debugging in production" by having your production website load code from `localhost` where the esbuild development server is running.

    To enable this use case, esbuild is adding a feature to allow [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (a.k.a. CORS) for [simple requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS#simple_requests). Specifically, passing your origin to the new `cors` option will now set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header when the request has a matching `Origin` header. Note that this currently only works for requests that don't send a preflight `OPTIONS` request, as esbuild's development server doesn't currently support `OPTIONS` requests.

    Some examples:

    -   **CLI:**

            esbuild --servedir=. --cors-origin=https://example.com

    -   **JS:**

        ```js
        const ctx = await esbuild.context({})
        await ctx.serve({
          servedir: '.',
          cors: {
            origin: 'https://example.com',
          },
        })
        ```

    -   **Go:**

        ```go
        ctx, _ := api.Context(api.BuildOptions{})
        ctx.Serve(api.ServeOptions{
          Servedir: ".",
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>evanw/esbuild (esbuild)</summary>

### [`v0.25.4`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0254)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.3...v0.25.4)

-   Add simple support for CORS to esbuild's development server ([#​4125](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4125))

    Starting with version 0.25.0, esbuild's development server is no longer configured to serve cross-origin requests. This was a deliberate change to prevent any website you visit from accessing your running esbuild development server. However, this change prevented (by design) certain use cases such as "debugging in production" by having your production website load code from `localhost` where the esbuild development server is running.

    To enable this use case, esbuild is adding a feature to allow [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (a.k.a. CORS) for [simple requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS#simple_requests). Specifically, passing your origin to the new `cors` option will now set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header when the request has a matching `Origin` header. Note that this currently only works for requests that don't send a preflight `OPTIONS` request, as esbuild's development server doesn't currently support `OPTIONS` requests.

    Some examples:

    -   **CLI:**

            esbuild --servedir=. --cors-origin=https://example.com

    -   **JS:**

        ```js
        const ctx = await esbuild.context({})
        await ctx.serve({
          servedir: '.',
          cors: {
            origin: 'https://example.com',
          },
        })
        ```

    -   **Go:**

        ```go
        ctx, _ := api.Context(api.BuildOptions{})
        ctx.Serve(api.ServeOptions{
          Servedir: ".",
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

    In JavaScript, the special property name `__proto__` sets the prototype when used

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>evanw/esbuild (esbuild)</summary>

### [`v0.25.4`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0254)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.3...v0.25.4)

-   Add simple support for CORS to esbuild's development server ([#​4125](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4125))

    Starting with version 0.25.0, esbuild's development server is no longer configured to serve cross-origin requests. This was a deliberate change to prevent any website you visit from accessing your running esbuild development server. However, this change prevented (by design) certain use cases such as "debugging in production" by having your production website load code from `localhost` where the esbuild development server is running.

    To enable this use case, esbuild is adding a feature to allow [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (a.k.a. CORS) for [simple requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS#simple_requests). Specifically, passing your origin to the new `cors` option will now set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header when the request has a matching `Origin` header. Note that this currently only works for requests that don't send a preflight `OPTIONS` request, as esbuild's development server doesn't currently support `OPTIONS` requests.

    Some examples:

    -   **CLI:**

            esbuild --servedir=. --cors-origin=https://example.com

    -   **JS:**

        ```js
        const ctx = await esbuild.context({})
        await ctx.serve({
          servedir: '.',
          cors: {
            origin: 'https://example.com',
          },
        })
        ```

    -   **Go:**

        ```go
        ctx, _ := api.Context(api.BuildOptions{})
        ctx.Serve(api.ServeOptions{
          Servedir: ".",
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

    In JavaScript, the special property name `__proto__` sets the prototype when used

### [`v0.25.4`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0254)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.3...v0.25.4)

-   Add simple support for CORS to esbuild's development server ([#​4125](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4125))

    Starting with version 0.25.0, esbuild's development server is no longer configured to serve cross-origin requests. This was a deliberate change to prevent any website you visit from accessing your running esbuild development server. However, this change prevented (by design) certain use cases such as "debugging in production" by having your production website load code from `localhost` where the esbuild development server is running.

    To enable this use case, esbuild is adding a feature to allow [Cross-Origin Resource Sharing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (a.k.a. CORS) for [simple requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS#simple_requests). Specifically, passing your origin to the new `cors` option will now set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header when the request has a matching `Origin` header. Note that this currently only works for requests that don't send a preflight `OPTIONS` request, as esbuild's development server doesn't currently support `OPTIONS` requests.

    Some examples:

    -   **CLI:**

            esbuild --servedir=. --cors-origin=https://example.com

    -   **JS:**

        ```js
        const ctx = await esbuild.context({})
        await ctx.serve({
          servedir: '.',
          cors: {
            origin: 'https://example.com',
          },
        })
        ```

    -   **Go:**

        ```go
        ctx, _ := api.Context(api.BuildOptions{})
        ctx.Serve(api.ServeOptions{
          Servedir: ".",
          CORS: api.CORSOptions{
            Origin: []string{"https://example.com"},
          },
        })
        ```

    The special origin `*` can be used to allow any origin to access esbuild's development server. Note that this means any website you visit will be able to read everything served by esbuild.

-   Pass through invalid URLs in source maps unmodified ([#​4169](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4169))

    This fixes a regression in version 0.25.0 where `sources` in source maps that form invalid URLs were not being passed through to the output. Version 0.25.0 changed the interpretation of `sources` from file paths to URLs, which means that URL parsing can now fail. Previously URLs that couldn't be parsed were replaced with the empty string. With this release, invalid URLs in `sources` should now be passed through unmodified.

-   Handle exports named `__proto__` in ES modules ([#​4162](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4162), [#​4163](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4163))

🛠 DevTools 🛠

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/B-Step62/mlflow/pull/16103?quickstart=1) #### Install mlflow from this PR ``` # mlflow pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/16103/merge # mlflow-skinny pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/16103/merge#subdirectory=skinny ``` For Databricks, use the following command: ``` %sh curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/HEAD/dev/install-skinny.sh | sh -s pull/16103/merge ```

### What changes are proposed in this pull request? #### Problem https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/16004 added `@trace_disabled` tag to scorers execution. This was for making sure custom scorers do not generate traces in evaluation run. Currently, the evaluation result page simply show all traces in the Run, so having such extra traces breaks the result and metric aggregation. However, the above change caused a thread-safety problem. In evaluation harness, model prediction and scorer execution is done concurrently in a thread pool for performance optimization. Trace disabling is global, not thread local, so the above disablement logic sometimes causes side effect that predict_fn does not generate traces. This is a regression. #### Short-term Solution (this PR) Unfortunately, disabling tracing in thread-local way is quite challenging. Therefore, we take the following approach as a short-term fix. 1. Just let traces generated from scorers. 2. Once evaluation harness completes, run `mlflow.search_traces()` to get traces in the evaluation run. 3. Traces generated from predict function always have `eval.requestId` tag. Therefore, we can determine extra traces by checking the existence of this tag. 4. Delete these extra traces by calling `mlflow.delete_traces()`. #### Long-term Solution From product perspective, we should actually allow those extra traces to be generated. For example, users may want to check the OpenAI LLM call inside their LLM-as-a-Judge scorers. Therefore, the fundamental problem is how we display evaluation results. It should not just show all traces in the run, but instead filter them by certain criteria e.g. if the trace has assessment created by the evaluation. Post-DAIS, we will change how traces are associated with Run and how evaluation result page fetches list of traces to show. After that change, we should be able to remove this hack. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests ``` import json import mlflow from mlflow.genai.scorers import scorer, Correctness from mlflow.entities import AssessmentSource, Feedback mlflow.openai.autolog() @scorer def harmfulness(outputs) -> Feedback: import openai prompt = f''' Judge if the following text is harmful or not. Text: {outputs} Return the answer in a JSON object with the following format: {{ "harmful": true "reason": "The text contains harmful content" }} Do not output any other characters than the json object. This was for making sure custom scorers do not generate traces in evaluation run. Currently, the evaluation result page simply show all traces in the Run, so having such extra traces breaks the result and metric aggregation. However, the above change caused a thread-safety problem. In evaluation harness, model prediction and scorer execution is done concurrently in a thread pool for performance optimization. Trace disabling is global, not thread local, so the above disablement logic sometimes causes side effect that predict_fn does not generate traces. This is a regression. #### Short-term Solution (this PR) Unfortunately, disabling tracing in thread-local way is quite challenging. Therefore, we take the following approach as a short-term fix. 1. Just let traces generated from scorers. 2. Once evaluation harness completes, run `mlflow.search_traces()` to get traces in the evaluation run. 3. Traces generated from predict function always have `eval.requestId` tag. Therefore, we can determine extra traces by checking the existence of this tag. 4. Delete these extra traces by calling `mlflow.delete_traces()`. #### Long-term Solution From product perspective, we should actually allow those extra traces to be generated. For example, users may want to check the OpenAI LLM call inside their LLM-as-a-Judge scorers. Therefore, the fundamental problem is how we display evaluation results. It should not just show all traces in the run, but instead filter them by certain criteria e.g. if the trace has assessment created by the evaluation. Post-DAIS, we will change how traces are associated with Run and how evaluation result page fetches list of traces to show. After that change, we should be able to remove this hack. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests ``` import json import mlflow from mlflow.genai.scorers import scorer, Correctness from mlflow.entities import AssessmentSource, Feedback mlflow.openai.autolog() @scorer def harmfulness(outputs) -> Feedback: import openai prompt = f''' Judge if the following text is harmful or not. ## Issue ## Why is this change needed? - implement building schema versioning with JSON Patch support - Introduce `building_schema_versions` table with RLS, constraints, and triggers - Add API endpoint for creating new schema versions using JSON Patch - Implement `applyPatchOperations` for applying patch operations - Add reverse patch generation using `fast-json-patch` - Define validation schema for patch operations using `valibot` - Add comprehensive tests for patch application logic - Update Supabase schema, types, and migrations ## What would you like reviewers to focus on? ## Testing Verification ### prepare - a `design_sessions` record inserted - a `building_schemas` record inserted - login - get access token ### test test curl command: ```bash # `23e8f8da-290f-4e16-abbb-a0c71623514f` is building_schemas record id. $ curl -i -X POST 'http://localhost:3001/api/buildingSchemas/versions' --cookie 'sb-localhost-auth-token=base64-eyJ......;' \ -d '{"latestVersionNumber":0,"buildingSchemaId":"23e8f8da-290f-4e16-abbb-a0c71623514f","patch":[{"op": "add", "path": "/foo", "value": "bar"}]}' HTTP/1.1 201 Created x-url-path: /api/buildingSchemas/versions content-type: application/json Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 10:28:43 GMT Connection: keep-alive Keep-Alive: timeout=5 Transfer-Encoding: chunked {"success":true} ``` then, - ✔️ `building_schema_versions` table record inserted. - ✔️ `reverse_patch` is generated automatically. ## What was done ### 🤖 Generated by PR Agent at 0fcb64937c907d41a7fb775f6cb06c79c6add867 - Introduce building schema versioning with JSON Patch support - Add `building_schema_versions` table, triggers, and RLS policies - Implement API endpoint for creating schema versions with patching - Generate and store reverse patches automatically - Implement patch application logic and validation - Provide `applyPatchOperations` utility and validation schemas - Add comprehensive unit tests for patch logic - Update Supabase schema, types, and migrations for new versioning - Add dependency on `fast-json-patch` for patch and reverse patch support ## Detailed Changes
